questions.stem: An 'invasive alien species' (IAS) is best defined as:

options.option_text: Any plant or animal not native to a region
A non-native species whose introduction causes economic or ecological harm
A native species that becomes dominant

questions.explanation: IUCN definition: an alien species whose introduction and spread threatens biological diversity, food security, plant/animal health or has economic and environmental impact. Key tests — (1) NON-native to the region, (2) ESTABLISHES self-sustaining populations, (3) causes HARM. Many alien species are harmless or beneficial (most crops). Only the harmful ones are 'invasive'. CBD's Aichi Target 9 and KMGBF Target 6 (2022) call on parties to identify, prioritise and control IAS pathways.

questions.stem: 'Lantana camara' — perhaps India's most damaging invasive plant — was introduced to India primarily as:

options.option_text: An ornamental garden plant in colonial era

questions.explanation: Lantana camara (native to South & Central America) was introduced into Calcutta Botanic Garden by the British in 1809 as an ornamental shrub for its colourful flowers. It escaped cultivation and now infests >40% of India's tiger reserves — outcompetes native vegetation, alters fire regimes, reduces forage for herbivores. Estimated economic damage: ₹900 crore/year. Hard to remove because it resprouts from root crowns; experiments include controlled burning + replanting natives.

questions.stem: 'Congress Grass' — a major weed associated with allergic dermatitis and hay fever in humans — is the common name for:
questions.explanation: Parthenium hysterophorus — also called 'gajar ghas' / 'Congress grass' (folklore says it arrived in India via PL-480 wheat aid during 1955-56). Causes contact dermatitis, asthma, hay fever in humans; toxic to cattle. Now infests ~35 million hectares across India. Biological control attempted using the leaf-feeding beetle Zygogramma bicolorata (Mexico). Eichhornia = water hyacinth. Mikania = mile-a-minute weed. Prosopis = mesquite (vilayati kikar).

questions.stem: Water Hyacinth (Eichhornia crassipes) is also nicknamed:
questions.explanation: Eichhornia crassipes — native to Amazon basin — introduced to India in the 1890s as an ornamental for ponds. Spread aggressively across Bengal waterways, choking fisheries and irrigation channels — hence 'Terror of Bengal'. It can double its biomass in two weeks under nutrient-rich conditions. Control methods — physical removal, herbicides (2,4-D), biological (Neochetina weevils). Some commercial uses — vermicompost, paper pulp, biogas — but elimination is far easier than utilisation.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an invasive ALIEN fish species banned from culture in India under guidelines from ICAR / FSSAI?

options.option_text: African Catfish (Clarias gariepinus) and Thai Mangur

questions.explanation: African / Thai Magur (Clarias gariepinus) — banned for culture in India since 2000 by NGT and reaffirmed by Supreme Court (2018). Reasons: (1) Outcompetes native magur (Clarias batrachus); (2) Carnivorous — eats native fish, frogs; (3) Grows fast in low-oxygen sewage water — biosecurity risk. Common Carp is naturalised; Catla, Rohu, Mrigal are native Indian Major Carps. Other banned exotics: Pacu (red-bellied piranha), Pirhana, Aligator gar.

questions.stem: 'Prosopis juliflora' — known in India as 'vilayati kikar' or 'angreji babool' — is an invasive species native to:
questions.explanation: Prosopis juliflora — drought-tolerant thorny tree from Mexico/Central America. Introduced to India in 1857 (Sind area, then Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu) for fuelwood and erosion control on degraded lands. It has now invaded grasslands and wetlands — depleting groundwater, replacing native flora. Punjabi name 'vilayati kikar' = 'foreign acacia'. In Tamil Nadu it covers >5 lakh ha. SC banned its felling without permits but TN and Rajasthan have programs to selectively remove it from biodiversity-sensitive areas.

questions.stem: Which Indian wildlife sanctuary is famously battling Mikania micrantha (mile-a-minute weed) that smothers native vegetation?
questions.explanation: Mikania micrantha — fast-growing climbing vine from Central/South America — was introduced to NE India in the 1940s to camouflage Allied airfields during WWII. It now smothers grasslands and bushes in Kaziranga, Manas and surrounding NE forests, reducing fodder for rhinos, elephants and deer. Manual uprooting is the main control. Other Kaziranga IAS concerns — water hyacinth, alligator weed (Alternanthera philoxeroides). Climate-change-aided spread is documented.
